dust.method: Vite bundles production Roost/MxDustMaterial and LocalAtmosphere into an isolated browser fixture. A deterministic mx450 snapshot emits dry roost for 40 updates at 1/60 s on real Valley Ridge terrain. Captures vary actual directional, hemisphere, point and spot lights, native fog and CSS/DPR dimensions while holding the emitted cloud. The atmosphere comparison translates cloud and camera together into authored pocket 0, installs twice, then checks clear, cloud=1/rain=20, held and disabled states. See the retained fixture for exact lamp parameters.

metricDefinitions.hash: 32-bit FNV-1a over 8-bit RGB readback bytes; alpha excluded for dust samples.
metricDefinitions.rgb: Sum of each 8-bit framebuffer channel across all pixels.
metricDefinitions.energy: Sum of RGB channel totals divided by width*height; display-space brightness metric, not physical radiance.
metricDefinitions.coverage: Fraction of pixels whose 8-bit R+G+B exceeds 9.
metricDefinitions.resources: Three.js renderer inventory after capture; resourceSet names the factored inventory for each sample.

limits: Controlled component test on Chromium/ANGLE SwiftShader, not a physical-GPU performance benchmark or a played race.
Aerial perspective adds one cached program when the production atmosphere hook first compiles; repeated hooked captures retain that inventory.
Black-background comparisons isolate dust response and do not establish full-scene artistic approval or optical calibration.
sourceUnchanged verifies the supplied simulation snapshot; the fixture does not measure human enjoyment or real-world scattering coefficients.

Dust uses a bounded point-particle lighting approximation with a fixed forward-scattering phase and averaged sky/ground illumination; it does not integrate a volumetric density field or particle self-shadowing.
dust.dprProtocol: 800x500 CSS at DPR 1 versus 400x250 CSS at DPR 2, both 800x500 physical pixels, followed by restoration.
